finding.claim: GlobalID.resolve_node embeds repr(node) in the ensure_type TypeError message, so a Node object of a different type (fetched via its resolve_node before the type check) is echoed to the client, bypassing field-level permission_classes on that object's fields.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied global ID (Relay id argument) on any user field that calls resolve_node(info, ensure_type=T); type prefix names a different Node type (strawberry/relay/utils.py:16-39; strawberry/relay/types.py:227-243 accepts any Node subclass).
finding.sink: strawberry/relay/types.py:207-212 (async) and strawberry/relay/types.py:311-314 (sync): f-string with {node!r} raised as TypeError.

trace.note: from_base64 decodes attacker ID into (type_name, node_id)
resolve_type looks up type by attacker-chosen name; accepts any Node subclass
n_type.resolve_node(...) runs and returns object of the other type before the type check
ensure_type isinstance check fails for the other type
non-Strawberry exceptions are coerced with str(error) and returned to the client; MaskErrors is opt-in

finding.guards_checked: resolve_type Node-subclass check (relay/types.py:239-243): stops non-Node types but not other Node types. ensure_type isinstance check (relay/types.py:207): blocks returning the object but not its repr. Field-level permission_classes: do not cover repr. Default error formatting: no masking unless MaskErrors configured. Verdict PLAUSIBLE: requires user code calling resolve_node(ensure_type=...) and a Node type whose resolve_node returns the object; impact depends on the type's __repr__ (dataclass-based Strawberry types include all fields).
